title: GPU rotation & driver rollforward plan (Sprint windows Q2 2025)
content:
Summary
This sheet is the sprint-aligned GPU rotation and driver rollforward plan for Q2 2025. Purpose is to coordinate staged capacity drains, validate driver 525.78 -> 531.12 rollforward across regions, and ensure SLA-preserving migration for hosted and dedicated customers. This plan focuses on low-latency pools, burst capacity, and downstream dependencies (KV cache format, vela autoscaler).

Goals
- Perform driver rollforward across all production GPU pools with zero data loss and <=1% request drop for hosted API traffic.
- Execute capacity drains so SRE can run node-level driver installs and reboot with predictable capacity impact.
- Validate per-region performance delta and capture fallback policies for canary regions.

Scope & Exclusions
- Includes: public hosted GPU pools (p1/p2/p3), dedicated pools scheduled in reserved maintenance windows, and edge region pools (us-west1, us-east4, eu-west2, ap-northeast1).
- Excludes: on-prem Private deployments unless specifically contracted (separate runbook).

Assumptions
- Continuous batching framework tolerates transient pod restarts (graceful drain 60s).
- KV cache persisted on NFS-backed store; warmup time ~3 minutes per node.
- Canary region (us-west1) has traffic split 0.5% for perf/regen tests.

High-level timeline (Q2 sprint cadence)
WindowID,Region,GPU Pool,Start (UTC),End (UTC),Planned Drain %,Affected Models,Driver Target,Owner,Slack Channel,Rollback Ticket

W2-USE4-1,us-east4,p1-lowlat,2025-05-13T01:00,2025-05-13T06:00,25%,gpt-4/gpt-3.5,531.12,Arjun P,#infra-maint,W-ROLL-002

W4-APN1-1,ap-northeast1,p2-burst,2025-05-27T00:00,2025-05-27T06:00,15%,all,531.12,Luca R,#infra-maint,W-ROLL-004
W5-REG-RESERVE,global,mixed,2025-06-03T00:00,2025-06-10T00:00,variable,non-critical,531.12,Oncall Team,#infra-maint,W-ROLL-005

Per-window checklist (runbook snippet)
- Pre-window (48h): notify customers (email + console banner), create canary datasets, snapshot KV caches. Attachments: maintenance-notice-template.
- Pre-window (4h): confirm capacity buffer >= 35% in same region or cross-region failover; run synthetic latency/throughput baseline.
- 30m before: set autoscaler min replicas to current-2 for rolling; pause autoscaler scale-up triggers for impacted pools.
- Drain sequence: drain node -> wait for in-flight token flush (60s) -> install driver -> soft-reboot container runtime -> smoke tests -> rejoin pool.
- Post-window (1h): remove maintenance banner, monitor 5-min P90 latency for 2 hours, run error budget check.

Capacity calculations (excerpt)
- us-west1 p1-lowlat pool: 120 GPUs, typical utilization 68% (tokens/sec), target drain 20% = 24 GPUs offline. Traffic migration required to other us-west1 pools + cross-region burst to us-east4 of up to 8 GPUs.
- us-east4 p1-lowlat pool: 200 GPUs, utilization 72%, planned drain 25% = 50 GPUs. Pre-provision reserve pool (burst) of 40 GPUs in dedicated-reserve. Remaining 10 GPUs handled by cross-region overflow to eu-west2 for short windows (<4 hours).

Risk matrix (top risks and mitigations)
- Driver incompatibility with optimized kernels -> Mitigation: canary in us-west1 with 0.5% traffic and perf diff gate (P95 latency delta <5% and token cost delta <2%). Abort if gate fails.
- KV cache deformation after upgrade -> Mitigation: snapshot and ability to restore node cache; fallback to cold-start with traffic throttling.
- Autoscaler misfire causing mass scale-down -> Mitigation: temporarily pin min replicas; on-call SRE watch.

Metrics to capture during and after
- Token throughput (tokens/s) per pool
- P50/P95 latency per model route
- Failed requests and 5-min error budget burn
- GPU memory usage and temperature distribution
- Driver kernel oops / containerd errors

Communication plan
- Pre-window: 48h automated email + tenant console banner. Templates in linked artifacts.
- During: Slack #infra-maint active thread, status updates every 30m. Pager escalation rule: >1% request drop triggers P1 on-call.
- Post: 1-page postmortem if any gate or rollback occurred; otherwise automated runbook closure note.

Rollback decision matrix
- Immediate rollback if: sustained P95 latency increase >20% for >10 minutes, or error rate spike >2% sustained 5 minutes, or driver kernel panic logged on >1 node within window.
- Rollback path: re-image nodes to previous driver 525.78 using staged image, bring nodes up in groups of 5, validate caches. Create rollback ticket linked in row.

Operational notes & edge cases
- Dedicated pools with customer pinning: schedule separately with Solutions Eng and include customer opt-in flag.
- Short windows (<4h) require tighter cross-region capacity reservations and must be approved by infra lead.
- If NFS latency during warm-up >250ms, pause rollforward and escalate to storage.

Open action items (owners)
- Pre-build driver image (531.12) with NVF userland patches: Arjun Patel (due 2025-04-22).
- Update autoscaler pause control to support one-off maintenance: Maya Hernandez (due 2025-04-24).
- Draft customer communication + console banner: Solutions Eng (Sophie Kim) (due 2025-04-25).

Notes for retrospective
- Capture actual per-node warmup times and KV cache hit recovery curves.
- Evaluate whether 60s graceful token flush needs to extend for long-tail LLMs.

Appendix (quick commands)
- Drain node: kubectl cordon NODE && kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
- Install driver job: ansible-playbook playbooks/gpu-driver-rollforward.yml -e driver_version=531.12 -e nodes=@nodes-list
- Smoke tests: scripts/bench-perf.sh --model gpt-4 --duration 120 --target 95th_threshold_ms=300

Revision history
- 2025-04-15: initial draft (Maya Hernandez)
- 2025-04-22: added capacity calc and reserve plan (Arjun Patel)
- 2025-05-02: updated rollback matrix and canary gate thresholds (Sophie Kim)

This sheet is intended to be used alongside the infra playbook and the driver compatibility matrix on Confluence. If you are planning a rollforward outside of these windows, coordinate with eng-infrastructure lead and SRE.
